rationale: The hypothesis that the electronegative ERG configuration in CLN3 retinopathy represents a stage-dependent inner retinal/bipolar cell signal transmission failure preceding total photoreceptor loss is supported across human clinical electrophysiology and genetic mouse models. Human pediatric and adult cohorts demonstrate that during earlier phases of disease, b-wave amplitudes are preferentially degraded relative to a-waves (producing an electronegative waveform in 100% of early-stage cohorts in Sakti et al. and 50% in the cohort of JNCL cases in Source [8], where the remaining 50% progressed to completely undetectable ERGs). Mechanistic studies in Cln3(Δex7/8) mice corroborate this timeline: bipolar cell dysfunction and rod bipolar cell degeneration occur before outer retinal photoreceptor loss, and inner retinal AAV gene replacement rescues retinal function whereas photoreceptor-targeted rescue fails.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 5 pediatric patients with confirmed CLN3 disease presenting at a median age of 6.2 years, visual electrophysiology showed electronegative ERGs in all 5 patients alongside early bull's-eye maculopathy and foveal ellipsoid zone disruptions.

evidence.text: In Cln3(Δex7/8) mice, the decline in inner retinal function and electronegative ERG response is caused by rod bipolar cell death, and inner retina-directed AAV gene delivery preserves bipolar cells and ERG function, whereas photoreceptor targeting is non-therapeutic because outer retinal loss occurs secondary to inner retinal disease.

source.quote: Cln3Δex7/8 mice, a mouse model of CLN3 Batten disease with juvenile onset, suffer from a decline in inner retinal function resulting from the death of rod bipolar cells... In contrast, the treatment of photoreceptors, which are lost in patients at late disease stages, was not therapeutic in Cln3Δex7/8 mice, underlining the notion that CLN3 disease is primarily a disease of the inner retina with secondary changes in the outer retina.

evidence.text: Review of ERGs in neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses showed that patients with JNCL exhibited severe ERG abnormalities with marked reduction of a-waves and disproportionately greater reduction of b-waves, producing an electronegative configuration reflecting failure of transmission from photoreceptors to second-order bipolar cells.

source.title: The dystrophic retina in multisystem disorders: the electroretinogram in neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses
source.quote: Patients with JNCL invariably showed severe to profound ERG abnormalities when first tested, with essentially no rod-mediated activity and marked loss of a-wave amplitudes with even greater loss of b-wave amplitudes, creating electronegative configuration waveforms.

evidence.text: Electronegative ERGs indicate a site of retinal dysfunction occurring post-phototransduction, particularly at the photoreceptor-to-bipolar cell synapse or in depolarizing bipolar cells, and variants in CLN3 are a recognized syndromic and non-syndromic cause.

new_directions.question_text: Does the transition from electronegative ERG to completely extinguished ERG in CLN3 patients correspond to secondary trans-synaptic photoreceptor degeneration or primary autonomous outer nuclear layer loss?
new_directions.rationale: While mouse gene therapy indicates inner retinal rescue is sufficient to maintain bipolar survival and ERG b-waves early on, human natural history studies show eventual undetectable ERGs with loss of outer retinal bands on OCT. Defining the precise temporal and structural dynamics between inner and outer retinal deterioration will inform optimal therapeutic windows.

new_directions.question_text: Can cellular-resolution inner retinal OCT imaging and peripheral blood vacuolated lymphocyte assays differentiate early CLN3 retinopathy from congenital stationary night blindness (CSNB) and X-linked retinoschisis (XLRS) presenting with electronegative ERGs?
new_directions.rationale: Electronegative ERG is shared by CSNB, XLRS, and melanoma-associated retinopathy; defining discriminatory non-invasive biomarkers (such as lymphocyte vacuolation and macular microcystic changes) will establish reliable differential diagnostic algorithms before onset of systemic neurodegeneration.
